title: tool call hydrator: idempotent result hydration, backpressure & retry contracts
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Tool-calling surfaces at Redwood are increasingly parallel and streaming-first. We observed two classes of production failures: transient upstream tool timeouts that caused duplicate downstream side-effects when clients retried, and streaming stalls when concurrent tool return envelopes were merged into the chat stream. This PR introduces a lightweight "tool hydrator" that provides an idempotent result injection contract, cooperative backpressure hooks for streaming response pipelines, and an explicit retry policy surface compatible with our OpenAI-compat layer.

Summary: This change implements: 1) a tool hydration protocol that attaches an idempotency key and deterministic merge hints to tool responses so replays are safe; 2) backpressure-aware streaming merge that signals the runtime to slow or batch late tool insertions instead of blocking the token stream; 3) a retry/hedging policy expressed as headers/metadata so the front-end and OpenAI-compat middleware can make consistent retry decisions; 4) unit + integration tests exercising parallel tool calls with simulated latency spikes and flaky tool endpoints.

Design notes (high-level): The hydrator is a small middleware between the invocation layer and the response serializer. It stamps tool responses with: - idempotency_key: client-provided or generated at invocation time - merge_strategy: one of [append, replace-on-timestamp, replace-on-seq] - schema_hint: short structured-output hint to improve downstream parsing (e.g., json-schema-id) We enforce an at-most-once injection into the streaming response by checking the idempotency_key within the request's KV cache and writing a short hydrated pointer into the stream instead of re-emitting duplicate payloads. For long-running tool results we emit a placeholder token ("[[tool-pending:<id>]]") and later hydrate the placeholder when the result arrives; hydration applies the merge_strategy for deterministic placement.

Retry contract: Retries are permitted only when the tool call returned an explicit transient error marker (transient=true) or when the idempotency_key is present. If the tool returns "uncertain" we include a replay token and require the caller to call back with explicit confirmation. Backoff defaults are conservative (exponential with jitter, min 100ms) and are surfaced via headers so the OpenAI-compat adapter can translate them to Retry-After semantics where appropriate.

Compatibility and migration: Default behavior is backwards compatible; we only add optional metadata fields to tool responses. Existing clients that ignore these fields will continue to receive tool payloads, but will not benefit from idempotent replays or hydration placeholders. The OpenAI-compat middleware is updated to consume retry headers and to prefer merge_strategy when converting tool results into choices/attachments.

Testing: Added unit tests for hydrator logic, integration tests that run 3 concurrent tool calls with synthetic delays and validate no duplicate side-effects, and an end-to-end smoke test with the OpenAI-compat adapter ensuring streaming stability under backpressure.

Checklist: - [x] Hydrator middleware implementation - [x] Streaming merge hooks and placeholder tokens - [x] Retry headers and policy translation - [x] Unit & integration tests - [x] Docs: API contract comment added to /docs/internal/tool-calls.md

Related work: builds on previous work to stabilize tool fanout (see ENG-1807) and complements the KV cache improvements from ENG-1982.

Notes: This is intentionally conservative on schema and merge heuristics; future PRs can add richer structured-output negotiation and eval-driven merge selection.

release_notes:
Features: Introduce tool hydrator middleware to enable idempotent tool result injections and placeholder hydration. Adds retry header surface for OpenAI-compat layer. Improvements: more resilient streaming merges under backpressure.
Migration: Backwards compatible; clients may opt-in to idempotency and merge strategies.
